html:
An intensifying conflict between the United States and Iran has become the most critical global development, with direct strikes, rising casualties, and significant economic implications. US forces launched a ninth night of strikes targeting Iran, while Iran escalated its attacks on US bases and regional targets, driving oil prices to their highest since June.

US-Iran Conflict: The United States confirmed the death of another service member in Iraq during a controlled detonation of an Iranian drone, following two US soldiers killed a day earlier in Jordan. These deaths bring the total number of US service members killed in recent days to three. Iran’s Revolutionary Guard claimed to have targeted US aircraft in Jordan and stopped two tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, vowing that not a "single drop" of oil or gas would pass without its approval. Iran's Army conducted drone strikes on US bases in Kuwait, targeting an ammunition depot and airbase, and also struck power and water plants in Kuwait, causing damage and injuries. Iran also launched missiles towards Jordan, with some intercepted, and attacked Bahrain. An under-construction nuclear plant in Iran was also reportedly hit by a US strike.

Russia-Ukraine War: Russia unleashed its largest ballistic missile assault of the war on Ukrainian cities, with 41 missiles and 125 drones hitting targets overnight, killing eight people and injuring dozens in Kyiv and other areas. Ukrainian forces continued their own assaults on Russian infrastructure. Meanwhile, Ukraine's struggle to recruit soldiers has intensified, with reports of aggression turning violent against recruitment officers.

Global Economy & Markets: The escalating US-Iran conflict pushed Brent crude oil prices above $90 a barrel, their highest since June, as markets braced for potential "all-out war." Concerns deepened with Iran's threats to halt oil transit through the Strait of Hormuz and reports of two ships suffering "accidents" there. Separately, the pay gap in the UK widened, with FTSE 100 chief executives receiving a median £5.06 million last year, 130 times the average worker's salary. In India, extreme heat is acting as a "poverty multiplier," causing outdoor workers to lose up to 9% of their income.

European Politics: Andy Burnham succeeded Keir Starmer as the United Kingdom’s new prime minister, pledging to "rewire Britain" with his politics shaped by England's north-south class divide. In environmental policy, a new EU ban on destroying unsold clothes, accessories, and footwear took effect, aimed at reducing waste. Wildfires continue to pose a threat, with a fast-moving blaze forcing evacuations in southern France and emergency crews battling another north of Madrid.

Global Security & Humanitarian Issues: Canada announced it would temporarily bar entry for foreign nationals who recently visited Congo, against UN advice, due to an Ebola risk. In the US, flash floods struck New York and New Jersey, inundating subway stations and streets. A flash flood in a Utah canyon tragically killed five family members. A 5.5-magnitude earthquake in Peru killed at least six people and displaced hundreds in the Andes region.

Regional Tensions: Israeli ministers joined a march to Gaza demanding the return of settlements, while Israeli settlers launched widespread attacks across the West Bank, burning homes and assaulting Palestinians. In Lebanon, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio praised Lebanon’s "move towards peace" after meeting President Joseph Aoun. Further south, the Yemen war reignited as Houthis threatened a blockade of the Bab Al-Mandab strait, raising fears of another critical oil chokepoint.
